pr_title: Fix Live coarse universe carrying over securities from previous day
pr_body:
#### Description
- The default value of `QCAlgorithm.UniverseSettings.MinimumTimeInUniverse` has been changed from `TimeSpan.FromDays(1)` to `TimeSpan.Zero`.

#### Related Issue
Closes #3287 

#### Motivation and Context
Live algorithms using Coarse universe selection were including symbols selected on the previous day.
This is caused by the fact that in Live mode Coarse universe selection is not triggered **exactly** at the same time every day, but it can happen several minutes before (or after) the 24-hour offset from the time of the previous day.

#### Requires Documentation Change
No.

#### How Has This Been Tested?
New unit test included.

issue_context.title: Live coarse universe may include securities from previous day
issue_context.body:
#### Expected Behavior
After Live coarse universe selection runs, we expect algorithm.ActiveSecurities to include only the securities selected (plus any security with open positions and orders).

#### Actual Behavior
Depending on the time Live coarse universe selection runs, securities which were selected previously may be kept in the universe (even if there are no open positions/orders).

#### Potential Solution
Update the default value of `QCAlgorithm.UniverseSettings.MinimumTimeInUniverse` from `TimeSpan.FromDays(1)` to `TimeSpan.Zero`.

#### Reproducing the Problem
Run a Coarse universe selection algorithm in Live mode for a week, logging the symbols selected by the coarse selection function and the symbols in `algorithm.ActiveSecurities` each day. 
On some days, securities from the previous day will be carried over to the next day.

#### System Information
n/a

comments: User reports another instance of this

review_comments: So it's now _impossible_ to set this to be greater than 1 day? I imagine some subset of users depend on the min time setting? I suppose the other way for a user to enforce a min time would be to manually track it in a local subscriptions list to feed back into the coarse selector. Is there a way to default the value to zero for coarse but permit it to be overridable?
I suspect this would be a breaking change for many user algorithms?
